title: Prove a cold first session registers on a small machine
text: Source tests prove the resident listens before it loads the evaluator; that a loading, never-listening or exiting resident holds the hook client no longer than YOKE_HOOK_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS (capped below the shortest harness hook timeout); that a spent budget allows the call with the shared degraded warning naming hook_budget_exhausted, the operator's own-terminal yoke hook resident restart and the YOKE_HOOKS_OFF switch; that a resident still loading exits at once on SIGTERM; and that stop escalates to SIGKILL for proven residents, names a still-running pid or a held start lock, and lets a restart accept a resident a live hook relaunched. yoke setup restarts the resident before the first harness session. The first live check on a 2 vCPU, 1 GB Linux test machine showed Codex ready on its first turn; under host memory pressure a later tool call refused with YOKE_HOOK_RESIDENT_TIMEOUT (infrastructure failures now fail open with that warning), and yoke hook resident restart timed out; the restart failure is fixed in source and the memory pressure is a host-admission matter outside the hook budget. Still owed: a live check on that machine that Cursor's first turn after yoke setup registers its session, and that a first hook after the ten-minute idle retirement answers inside Cursor's 30-second hook timeout.
